n: Algernon Sidney Gilbert, a Kirtland merchant and business partner of Newel K. Whitney, had prayed to know his place in the restored Church. The Lord tells him his prayers are heard.

f.g: Algernon Sidney Gilbert (1789–1834), who later ran the Church store in Independence, Missouri.
Here, his assignment and role in the Church.

n: The Savior, identifying himself as the one crucified for the world’s sins, asks Sidney to forsake the world—to put worldly pursuits second to God’s work.
He is to be ordained an elder to preach faith, repentance, forgiveness of sins, and the gift of the Holy Ghost—the first principles and ordinances of the gospel.

f.w: faith and repentance and remission of sins

n: He will also be an agent for the Church, handling business affairs where the bishop directs. His business skills are put to sacred use.
He is to travel to Missouri with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon.
These are his first assignments; more will come according to his faithful labor. Callings unfold over time.
Finally: only those who endure to the end are saved. Gilbert served faithfully until he died of cholera in Missouri in 1834.

f.w: he only is saved who endureth unto the end
